candidate.answerReason: Each day leaves 80% of the starting amount. Working backward from 32 gives 32/0.8 = 40 and then 40/0.8 = 50.

methods.label: Work backward one day at a time
methods.explanation:
Eating \(20\%\) leaves \(80\%=0.8\) of the jellybeans present at the beginning of that day. To recover a day's starting amount from its remaining amount, divide by \(0.8\).

Thus the number at the beginning of the second day was
\[
32\div0.8=40.
\]
Those \(40\) jellybeans were what remained after the first day, so the original number was
\[
40\div0.8=50.
\]
Starting with \(50\), Jenny eats \(10\) on the first day and \(8\) on the second, leaving \(32\) as required. The answer is \(\boxed{50}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Successive inverse-percentage calculations use elementary percentage interpretation and decimal division.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is recovering an unknown whole from a known percentage, applied twice. Percentage conversion and the part-to-whole division relationship support that target. Decimal division supplies the local numerical calculation; a geometric-sequence model is unnecessary.

review.mathematicalCheck: Each day retains 0.8 of its starting count. Reversing twice gives 32 ÷ 0.8 = 40 and 40 ÷ 0.8 = 50; the forward check leaves exactly 32 whole jellybeans.
